# dsh-connect-two

One panel for the credits and daily check-in of your locally signed-in
**Trae** and **WorkBuddy** ac
counts, with an **opt-in** daily automatic check-in.

> A **companion bundle**, not a fork. `dsh-connect-trae` and
> `dsh-connect-workbuddy` stay installe

d and keep receiving upstream updates;
> this plugin only reads their read-only routes and calls the

check-in route
> they already ship.
## Why not merge the two plugins
| | A. Companion bundle (this) | B. Merge into one plugin |

| One panel for both apps | ✅ | ✅ |
| Upstream keeps updating | ✅ upgrade directly | ❌ permanently d

iverged |
| Maintenance cost | ~500 lines | fork two 1.4 MB builds, 100+ sources |
| After uninstall
ing | both plugins keep working | you own all of it |

Both upstream plugins iterate fast (4.6.12 / 5.17.0 locally while upstream had
already shipped 4.7.0

/ 5.18.0). Merging means hand-porting every release from
then on, so this is a companion instead.
## What it does

- **Unified panel** under Settings → Plugins → "Check-in & Credits": the four
panels (Trae CN / Glob

al, WorkBuddy CN / Global) with sign-in state, available
and total credits, today's check-in state,

and streak length.
- **Check in all / check in one**: shown only for the **domestic** side, because

the global sides have no check-in activity at all.
- **Daily automatic check-in**: off by default. W

hen enabled you choose the run
time, which apps it covers, and whether a missed slot is caught up on

the next
start.
- **Check-in log**: manual and scheduled runs are both recorded, each row saying
cl
aimed / already claimed / device quota used / failed.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or once published to npm:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A successful install reports `application: "applied"`. **Host-side changes need
a `dsh web` restart*
* to load; the Client half hot-reloads.
## Usage

1. Settings → Plugins → **Check-in & Credits**.
2. The rows are live; **Refresh** re-reads them.
3.

**Check in all**, or the per-row **Check in**, claims today's reward now.
4. For automatic check-in,

turn the switch on, set the time, pick the apps.
The scheduler runs while the Harness process is up

; a slot missed while it
was down only executes if **Catch up missed runs** is enabled.
## Safety notes

- Check-in is the only operation that changes upstream account state, and it is
driven only by your

button press or by a schedule you explicitly enabled.
- Both routes are loopback-only. The Hub addit

ionally checks the `Host` header,
so a foreign origin or a DNS-rebinding host is refused with 403.
-

Repeated claims are harmless: both upstream plugins read today's status first
and answer `alreadyCh

eckedIn` instead of claiming twice.
- A run where **every** target failed does not mark the day as d

one, so the slot
stays open and retries. A partially successful run does mark it.
## State

- `$DSH_HOME/dsh-connect-two/state.json` — config, log (last 200 entries), and
the day of the last a

utomatic run.
- Delete it to return to defaults (automatic check-in off).
- Config validation lives

in one place; an invalid time is normalised back to a
legal value instead of being stored.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Layout: `src/` holds the plugin (the package root manifest points into it),
`test/` the contract tes
ts, `docs/` the design notes and the measured log.
## Boundaries (stated plainly)

- Check-in exists on the **domestic side only**. The global sides show credits
but no check-in butto

n, because their upstream has no such activity.
- WorkBuddy **enterprise / education** seats are ref

used by the upstream write
API (`10001`); those rows report failure as failure rather than faking su

ccess.
- Automatic check-in depends on the Harness process being alive at the chosen
time, unless ca

tch-up is enabled.
- The panel has not been visually reviewed in a browser by this repository's
auth

or; styling uses only `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens so it follows the host
light/dark theme.
